adjudication_records.issue_text: assignment_source.py: should use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` instead of a mutable default call

adjudication.rationale: In `AssignmentSource` the dataclass field `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` calls `timezone.now()` at import/class definition time, so every `AssignmentSource()` created without an explicit `queued` will get the same frozen timestamp (not “now” at instantiation). The correct pattern is `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` to evaluate per-instance.

adjudication_records.issue_text: to_dict() uses asdict() which leaves `queued` as a datetime object, not JSON-serializable

adjudication.rationale: In `AssignmentSource.to_dict()`, `asdict(self)` will indeed include `queued` as a `datetime` object (`queued: datetime = timezone.now()`), so the produced dict is not JSON-serializable as-is. This dict is then passed through Celery (`sync_group_assignee_outbound` -> `sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async(... assignment_source_dict=...)`). The diff does not show what serializer Celery uses in this project (pickle vs JSON), so it's not verifiably broken from the diff alone, but it is a concrete, diff-grounded risk/concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: sync_assignee_outbound.py:62: `should_sync` called with new positional argument `parsed_assignment_source`, breaking every should_sync override not updated to the new signature

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the method signature of `IssueBasicIntegration.should_sync` (and `IssueSyncIntegration.should_sync`) to accept a second parameter `sync_source: AssignmentSource | None`, and `sync_assignee_outbound` now calls `installation.should_sync("outbound_assignee", parsed_assignment_source)` with that new positional argument. If there are any other `should_sync` overrides elsewhere in the codebase that still have the old `(attribute)` signature, this call would raise a `TypeError` at runtime. The diff itself doesn’t show whether such other overrides exist, so the breakage can’t be confirmed from the provided changes alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: from_dict performs no type coercion, so Celery-JSON round-trip yields `queued` as a string inside a datetime-typed field

adjudication.rationale: In `AssignmentSource` (`src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py`), `to_dict()` uses `asdict(self)` which will include `queued` as a `datetime` object, while `from_dict()` simply does `cls(**input_dict)` with no parsing/coercion. If the dict is serialized/deserialized (e.g., through Celery kwargs in `sync_group_assignee_outbound` -> `apply_async` passing `assignment_source_dict`), a JSON round-trip would typically turn a datetime into a string; `from_dict` would then accept that string into the `queued: datetime` field without complaint. The diff doesn’t show `queued` being used yet (only `integration_id` is checked in `should_sync`), so it’s not a clearly manifested runtime bug in this PR, but it is a concrete, diff-grounded type/serialization concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: groupassignee.py: top-level import of assignment_source into a region-silo core model file reverses the established dependency direction and couples the model layer to the integrations package

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `src/sentry/models/groupassignee.py` (a `region_silo_model` core model file) now has a new top-level import `from sentry.integrations.services.assignment_source import AssignmentSource`. Previously, integration-related imports in this file were done inside methods (e.g., `from sentry.integrations.utils import sync_group_assignee_outbound` within `assign`/`deassign`), which avoids hard module-level coupling. This change concretely increases dependency from the model layer into the `sentry.integrations` package and can be considered an architectural/dependency-direction concern, though it is not a directly verifiable runtime defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: sync_assignee_outbound task passes assignment_source kwarg but abstract method signature in mixins/issues.py was never updated to accept it, causing TypeError with provider implementations lacking **kwargs

adjudication.rationale: In `sync_assignee_outbound` task, the call to `installation.sync_assignee_outbound(...)` was changed to pass a new keyword argument `assignment_source=parsed_assignment_source` (see `src/sentry/integrations/tasks/sync_assignee_outbound.py`). In `mixins/issues.py`, the diff updates `should_sync(...)` and the abstract `sync_status_outbound(...)` signature to accept an `AssignmentSource`, but does not show any corresponding update to the `sync_assignee_outbound` abstract method signature. If provider implementations of `sync_assignee_outbound` don’t accept `assignment_source` (or `**kwargs`), this new kwarg will raise a `TypeError` at runtime.

adjudication_records.issue_text: assignment_source.to_dict() uses dataclasses.asdict leaving queued as datetime, which is not JSON-serializable for apply_async with JSON serializer, causing EncodeError at enqueue time

adjudication.rationale: In `AssignmentSource.to_dict()` (new file `assignment_source.py`), `dataclasses.asdict(self)` will include `queued` as a `datetime` object. That dict is passed through Celery `apply_async` as `assignment_source_dict` in `sync_group_assignee_outbound()` (`integrations/utils/sync.py`). If Celery is configured to use a JSON serializer for task kwargs, a raw `datetime` is not JSON-serializable and would raise an encode error when enqueuing the task. The diff shows no conversion of `queued` to a string/epoch before enqueueing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AssignmentSource dataclass field default queued: datetime = timezone.now() is evaluated once at class-definition time, so all instances share the import-time timestamp

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py`, the dataclass defines `queued: datetime = timezone.now()`. This calls `timezone.now()` at import/class-definition time, so every `AssignmentSource()` created without an explicit `queued` value will reuse the same frozen timestamp, rather than getting the creation time. A correct pattern would be `field(default_factory=timezone.now)`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Cycle prevention applied only to should_sync('outbound_assignee'); status sync loops (outbound_status, sync_status_inbound) are unprotected, allowing ping-pong the PR claims to prevent

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds cycle-prevention logic in `IssueSyncIntegration.should_sync(..., sync_source)` by returning False when `sync_source.integration_id == self.org_integration.integration_id`. However, in the shown changes this new `sync_source` is only parsed/passed for assignee outbound (`sync_assignee_outbound` task calls `installation.should_sync("outbound_assignee", parsed_assignment_source)` and passes `assignment_source` onward). While `sync_status_outbound`’s signature is extended to accept `assignment_source`, the diff does not show any caller passing an `AssignmentSource` into status sync or using `should_sync` with a source for status-related attributes. So the finding that only outbound assignee is protected is supported by the diff; whether this is a “bug” depends on intended scope, which isn’t verifiable here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: from_dict returns None on any TypeError including forward-compatible payloads with extra keys, silently disabling cycle guard during rolling deploy skew

adjudication.rationale: In `AssignmentSource.from_dict`, parsing is `cls(**input_dict)` and any `TypeError` returns `None` (e.g., unexpected keyword args from extra keys). That means if the task payload ever includes additional fields (e.g., during a rolling deploy with mixed versions or future schema expansion), `parsed_assignment_source` becomes `None` in `sync_assignee_outbound`, and `installation.should_sync("outbound_assignee", parsed_assignment_source)` will not apply the cycle-prevention check (`if sync_source and ...`). This is a diff-grounded forward/compatibility concern rather than a currently-triggered defect because the diff doesn’t show any extra keys being sent today beyond the dataclass fields.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No test for deassign with assignment_source, leaving inbound-unassign loop guard unverified

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a loop-guard via `IssueSyncIntegration.should_sync(..., sync_source)` that prevents outbound sync when `sync_source.integration_id == self.org_integration.integration_id` (src/sentry/integrations/mixins/issues.py). `GroupAssignee.deassign(..., assignment_source=...)` now propagates `assignment_source` through `sync_group_assignee_outbound` into the `sync_assignee_outbound` task, which uses `installation.should_sync("outbound_assignee", parsed_assignment_source)` (src/sentry/integrations/tasks/sync_assignee_outbound.py). Tests cover the guarded *assign* path (`test_assignee_sync_outbound_assign_with_matching_source_integration` asserts no outbound call), but there is no corresponding test for `GroupAssignee.objects.deassign(..., assignment_source=AssignmentSource.from_integration(integration))` to ensure outbound unassign is similarly suppressed. This is a specific missing test for newly added nontrivial behavior, not a proven functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Inbound path lacks end-to-end test (webhook to should_sync returning False for same integration); tests stop at model layer

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new cycle-prevention logic based on `AssignmentSource` flowing from inbound assignment into outbound sync (`sync_group_assignee_inbound` now calls `GroupAssignee.objects.assign/deassign(... assignment_source=AssignmentSource.from_integration(integration))`, and `IssueSyncIntegration.should_sync(..., sync_source)` returns False when `sync_source.integration_id` matches `self.org_integration.integration_id`). Tests were added for `AssignmentSource` serialization and for the outbound path when `GroupAssignee.objects.assign(... assignment_source=...)` is called, but there is no test exercising the actual inbound helper `sync_group_assignee_inbound` (i.e., the inbound entrypoint that sets the assignment_source) end-to-end. That’s a concrete coverage gap for the newly added inbound propagation behavior, even though related logic is partially covered via model-layer invocation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: from_dict performs no coercion, so queued becomes a str while typed datetime after JSON round-trip, causing TypeError on staleness comparisons

adjudication.rationale: In `AssignmentSource`, `to_dict()` uses `asdict(self)` which includes `queued` as a `datetime` object, and the value is passed through Celery task kwargs as `assignment_source_dict` (`sync_group_assignee_outbound` -> `sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async`). If this dict is JSON-serialized/deserialized, `queued` would become a string, and `from_dict()` does no parsing/coercion (`return cls(**input_dict)`), so instances could end up with `queued` as a `str` despite the annotation. However, in this diff `queued` is never used (only `integration_id` is checked in `should_sync`), and no “staleness comparisons” exist here, so the claimed TypeError isn’t directly verifiable from the shown changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: queued field default timezone.now() evaluated once at class-definition time, freezing the same timestamp for all AssignmentSource instances for the process lifetime; should use field(default_factory=timezone.now)

adjudication.rationale: In `AssignmentSource` (new file `src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py`), the dataclass field is defined as `queued: datetime = timezone.now()`. This calls `timezone.now()` at import/class definition time, so every `AssignmentSource()` created without an explicit `queued` will get the same frozen timestamp for the process lifetime. For per-instance timestamps it should be `queued: datetime = field(default_factory=timezone.now)`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: to_dict() emits raw datetime for queued which is passed as a Celery apply_async kwarg, causing a serialization error under the JSON serializer so outbound sync tasks are never enqueued

adjudication.rationale: `AssignmentSource.to_dict()` uses `dataclasses.asdict(self)` (new file `assignment_source.py`), which will include the `queued` field as a raw `datetime`. That dict is passed directly into `sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async(kwargs={... "assignment_source_dict": assignment_source.to_dict() ...})` in `integrations/utils/sync.py`. If Celery is using a JSON serializer (common/default in many setups), a `datetime` inside kwargs is not JSON-serializable, so enqueueing the task can fail at serialization time. The diff shows no conversion (e.g., ISO string) for `queued`, and the added test only asserts it is "not None", not serializable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: from_dict calls cls(**input_dict) where queued arrives as a string with no validation, silently corrupting the datetime type invariant

adjudication.rationale: In `AssignmentSource.from_dict`, the code does `return cls(**input_dict)` without parsing/validating field types (notably `queued`). Since Python dataclasses don’t enforce type hints at runtime, if `queued` is present in `input_dict` as a string (a plausible outcome when passing through task serialization), an `AssignmentSource` instance would be created with `queued` as a string rather than a `datetime`, and this would not raise `ValueError`/`TypeError`. However, within this diff `queued` is not used anywhere for logic (only `integration_id` is checked in `should_sync`), so it’s not a directly verifiable broken behavior yet—more of a robustness/typing issue in newly added code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: assignment_source propagation is only wired through the assignee path; status sync and comment sync inbound paths never construct or thread an AssignmentSource, leaving sync cycles unprevented for status changes

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `AssignmentSource` and a cycle-prevention check in `IssueSyncIntegration.should_sync(..., sync_source=...)`, but only the assignee outbound/inbound flow actually constructs/parses/passes it (`sync_group_assignee_inbound` -> `GroupAssignee.assign/deassign(...assignment_source=...)` -> `sync_group_assignee_outbound(...assignment_source=...)` -> task parses `assignment_source_dict` and passes to `installation.should_sync(...)`). Although `sync_status_outbound`’s signature is extended to accept `assignment_source`, this diff does not show any status/comment sync callsites being updated to pass an `AssignmentSource`, so the new cycle-prevention mechanism is not generally applied beyond the assignee path. This is an incompleteness/scope issue, not a verifiable broken behavior introduced here (defaults keep existing calls working).

adjudication_records.issue_text: sync_status_outbound gains an assignment_source parameter that no call site passes or consumes — dead implementation surface that should be removed or properly threaded

adjudication.rationale: In this diff, only the abstract method signature `IssueSyncIntegration.sync_status_outbound(...)` is expanded to include `assignment_source: AssignmentSource | None = None` (src/sentry/integrations/mixins/issues.py), but no corresponding threading of that parameter is shown (unlike the assignee path, where `assignment_source` is parsed/passed and used in `should_sync`). From the diff alone, this new parameter is not consumed anywhere and no call sites are updated, so it appears to be unused API surface unless other (not-shown) code passes it.

adjudication_records.issue_text: should_sync base-class signature change (sync_source param) silently breaks cycle suppression for any IssueBasicIntegration subclass that overrides should_sync without forwarding sync_source, with no contract update or documentation of the new obligation

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the method signature of `IssueBasicIntegration.should_sync` to accept an optional `sync_source` (`issues.py`), and call sites now pass that second argument (e.g. `sync_assignee_outbound` calls `installation.should_sync("outbound_assignee", parsed_assignment_source)`). While `IssueSyncIntegration` is updated accordingly, the diff does not show whether all other `IssueBasicIntegration`/installation subclasses that override `should_sync` were updated. If any override still has the old `(attribute)` signature, this API change can break those implementations (likely via a `TypeError` at runtime, or by not applying cycle-prevention logic if they reimplement `should_sync` without considering `sync_source`). The finding’s “silently breaks cycle suppression” phrasing isn’t directly verifiable from the diff, but the contract-change risk is diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: dataclass field default `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` in assignment_source.py is evaluated once at import time, so every AssignmentSource gets the process-start timestamp instead of enqueue time

adjudication_records.issue_text: assignment_source.to_dict() embeds a datetime in Celery task kwargs, which will raise TypeError if the task moves to a JSON/JSONBytes queue

adjudication.rationale: In `sync_group_assignee_outbound` the task is enqueued with `assignment_source_dict=assignment_source.to_dict()` (utils/sync.py). `AssignmentSource.to_dict()` returns `asdict(self)`, which includes the `queued: datetime` field (assignment_source.py). A `datetime` is not JSON-serializable by default, so if Celery uses a JSON/JSONBytes serializer for this task/queue, serialization would fail (TypeError). The diff doesn’t show what serializer is currently configured, so it’s a concrete risk introduced here but not definitively a broken behavior in this PR.
